System A:
  Clarity: 8.3/10
  Engagement: 7.6/10
  Depth Appropriateness: 8.5/10
  Breadth: 8.7/10
System B:
  Clarity: 7.4/10
  Engagement: 6.5/10
  Depth Appropriateness: 6.8/10
  Breadth: 6.9/10
System C:
  Clarity: 7.8/10
  Engagement: 6.7/10
  Depth Appropriateness: 7.2/10
  Breadth: 7.5/10

Explanation:
[A|Clarity]: Round 1 Instructor answer explains exploration efficiency through a concrete mechanism — "Chest income is basically chest density times accessibility (no climbing or stamina detours) times how much puzzle overhead each chest carries" — and Round 3's crit-ratio answer derives the 1:2 rule from "the average damage multiplier is CR × CD, and for a fixed total budget that product is largest when crit rate is half of crit damage," then names each hidden assumption individually. Transitions between rounds are signposted by the Extension lines (e.g., "Energy Recharge thresholds are the quiet gate on all of this"). Minor gap: some numeric anchors (e.g., "roughly 180–220% ER") are presented as starting values without always showing the underlying particle math in the user-facing text.

[A|Engagement]: The student's selected questions track the user's intent closely — Round 1 selects an exploration-efficiency question matching "Genshin Impact strategies," Round 2 selects an ER-threshold question matching "enhance performance," and Round 3 selects a crit-assumption question. Each Instructor answer closes with an "Extension" that hands the user a concrete next concept (energy funneling, rotation-specific minimum, "which multiplier your character's damage actually flows through"). Gap: the user never supplies mid-process input after the initial prompts, so engagement is largely system-initiated rather than a genuine back-and-forth.

[A|Depth Appropriateness]: Foundations are established before complexity — Round 1 builds the five-layer framework first, Round 2 introduces ER as "rotation-specific minimums" with archetype anchors (National, Hyperbloom, Freeze), and Round 3 escalates to the joint ATK/crit curve "y = 75*(100/B + B/50) - 100" only after the simple 1:2 heuristic is explained. Numbers are consistently framed as anchors to verify ("treat them as starting points to verify in-game, not laws"), which appropriately handles uncertainty about user expertise. Minor gap: the final summary's pull-budget figures (e.g., "F2P ~7 gold as 3+3+1") appear without explanation of what "gold" or the split notation means.

[A|Breadth]: The interaction develops five genuinely distinct and connected dimensions — builds, teams, resources, combat, exploration — and the final summary explicitly relates them ("builds determine what a character can do, teams determine what four characters can do together..."). Round 3 adds a real tension (crit builds vs. EM triggers: "a Hyperbloom trigger's damage ignores crit entirely, so a 1:2 crit build on Kuki... is close to wasted resin") rather than just listing subtopics. Gap: combat mechanics and encounter-specific tactics (shield-breaking, positioning, boss gimmicks) are named in the bootstrap but never developed in any round's user-facing answer.

[B|Clarity]: Round 1's General Knowledge Provider answer explains roles with functional definitions ("Main DPS (on-field carry triggering reactions set up by supports), Sub-DPS (off-field damage whose skills/bursts stay active after switching)"), and Round 3's speedrunner answer enumerates resonance effects with concrete values (Pyro "flat 25% ATK," Cryo "15% CRIT Rate against Cryo-affected or frozen enemies"). Gap: Round 2's answer is largely a restatement of Round 1's Game8 material with the same Hydro Hypostasis example, so the "big lever for performance" framing adds little explanatory progression; the closing summary's Venti–Xiangling section introduces snapshotting and Viridescent Venerer mechanics without explaining them.

[B|Engagement]: The warm-start moderator questions ("what does your ideal cycle look like from support setup to particle funneling?") and Round 3's invitation-style framing attempt to involve the reader, and the answers connect to concrete team scenarios (Venti–Xiangling, single-target adaptation). Gap: the actual user turns ("Genshin Impact strategies," "Identify and analyze effective gameplay strategies") receive answers that are broad overviews rather than responses to any user contribution, and Round 3 proceeds autonomously ("No new user input; autonomous continuation") with no mechanism for the user to steer.

[B|Depth Appropriateness]: Round 3's investment answer distinguishes vertical vs. horizontal investment with reasons ("pulling a niche dedicated support for one specific team is functionally vertical investment, not horizontal") and Round 1's resonance answer gives specific stat values. Gap: depth stays at guide-summary level throughout — Round 2's answer repeats Round 1's team-building basics nearly verbatim rather than deepening, and no round develops mechanisms like ICD, snapshotting, or particle math despite these being consequential to the stated goal of "enhancing performance."

[B|Breadth]: The record covers team-building fundamentals, elemental resonance (all eight types enumerated in Round 3), the Venti–Xiangling pairing, single-target adaptation, and investment strategy (vertical vs. horizontal) — five relevant dimensions with some relationships drawn (resonance as a team-building layer; investment trade-offs). Gap: coverage is uneven — artifact optimization, energy management, and rotation execution are explicitly flagged as out of scope in Round 2 ("this covers team-building fundamentals only, not artifact optimization or rotation execution") and never revisited, leaving major performance levers undeveloped.

[C|Clarity]: Round 2's answer explains why artifact consolidation works with a mechanism — "damage is multiplicative across ATK, crit, and elemental bonuses. A single strong piece misplaced on an unused character contributes nothing" — and Round 3 explains animation canceling precisely: "final attack frames consume time, but damage is registered at the moment of impact." Round 1's daily-habits section is plainly actionable. Gap: Round 2's energy section lists tactics (funneling, resonance) without walking through an example of a rotation where they apply, so the connection between "particles feed the on-field character" and a concrete swap sequence is left implicit.

[C|Engagement]: Each round responds directly to the prompt's framing — Round 1 answers "Genshin Impact strategies" with a routine, Round 2 answers "identify and analyze" with a three-method analysis, Round 3 answers "what else should I know" with two new layers — and Round 3's table explicitly connects back to earlier rounds ("Combine layers: animation canceling + correct ER + a team built around the floor's disorder"). Practical takeaways ("Practice animation canceling on your main DPS first") give the user actionable entry points. Gap: no turn invites or accommodates user response; the process is three independent prompt-response pairs rather than a developing dialogue.

[C|Depth Appropriateness]: Foundations precede complexity: Round 1 covers daily habits before Round 2 introduces multiplicative damage and particle mechanics, and Round 3 adds execution-level detail only after build and team layers exist. Round 2's layered team-building theory (damage → rotation → energy/survival) provides a reasonable conceptual scaffold. Gap: several consequential claims stay at assertion level — "ER should be tuned per character (burst-reliant supports often need 180–250%)" gives a range without showing how it's derived, and Ley Line Disorder implications are illustrated with Floor 5 but the general method for evaluating other disorders isn't developed.

[C|Breadth]: The final framework table names six layers (mechanical, environmental, build, team, resource, foundational) and the cross-cutting principles section relates them ("Concentrate resources," "Fix the bottleneck"). Distinct dimensions — daily routine, artifact consolidation, energy, team theory, animation canceling, Abyss disorders, exploration — are each explained enough to convey their contribution. Gap: gacha/wish management and exploration receive only brief treatment (Round 1 lists pity thresholds and interactive-map use in a few lines) and are not connected to the performance-analysis theme of Rounds 2–3, so those dimensions remain thin relative to the build/team/mechanical layers.
